findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the ItemRecord adapter maps the code-review-verify arm's `{verifications:[...]}` output to a coarse decision (verifications present/absent → block/advisory), or exclude the code-review-verify spec from the corpus, since `_verdict_decision` as written scores every verify case `advisory` regardless of gold label.
evidence: `_verdict_decision` at src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:83-86 keys only on `out.get('verdict')=='FAIL'` or `out.get('findings')`; a `{verifications:[...]}` output yields neither, so it returns `advisory`.

`_run_code_review_case` docstring at src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:217-218: 'a base/overlay reviewer's {findings:[...]} ... or the verifier's {verifications:[...]}' — the verify arm's native output has no `findings`/`verdict` key.

code-review-verify.eval.yaml lines 24-27 & 40-43: `V-real-defect expect: finding` (gold=block) and `V-clean-rename expect: pass` — both eligible under the plan's rule (expect in {finding,pass}, non-agentic code-review arm).

The committed src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json empirically confirms the miss: `V-real-defect` has `label: block` but `decision: advisory` on BOTH v1 and v2 in both slots (lines 316-330, 854-868).
findings.finding: The plan reuses `fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision` as THE decision rule for all pooled arms and calls it 'the same two-bucket mapping', but that rule reads only the `verdict`/`findings` keys and does not handle the `code-review-verify` arm's `{verifications:[...]}` output vocabulary — which the plan's own eligibility rule admits — so every verify case is scored `advisory`, forcing a guaranteed recall miss on its gold-block case.
findings.location: Approach → 'Corpus and the gold floor' ("the same two-bucket mapping fidelity_spot_eval._verdict_decision already uses") and Scope → provider_parity.py 'the epoch-majority ItemRecord adapter'
scenarios: Any measured slot whose corpus includes a code-review-verify case: the verify recall case scores advisory on both arms, distorting recall/false-accept and masking a real regression as agreement.
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend the adapter to treat a non-empty `verifications` list as `block` (mirroring the presence contract code-review-verify.eval.yaml scores on), or add code-review-verify to the excluded-spec set alongside the three agentic ops; whichever is chosen, state it in the adapter's worked example so the verify output shape is handled explicitly.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

verify command `grep -rnE '\bprovider_parity\b' .github/workflows/` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

evidence: Prerequisite: 'Decision A — the default is `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, the verified-caching regional inference profile.'
Prerequisite: opus-4-5 'silently do not cache'
Subject frontier slot: 'bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8' asserted to do 'most of the gate's work'
findings.finding: The prerequisite (S3) MEASURED and documented `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` as the caching default and explicitly recorded that `us.`/`global.` opus-4-5 silently do NOT cache, with caching being MODEL-dependent. The subject plan's `frontier` slot uses `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` and asserts it does most of the gate's work as the Pass-1 finder, but neither the subject nor the prerequisite has measured whether opus-4-8 caches. More directly incompatible: the prerequisite states (Decision C, verified) that both current opus candidates `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` and `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` carry `supports_temperature: False`, and the subject plan relies on exactly this (`capabilities.py:126-129`). The subject and prerequisite agree on the temperature-override mechanism. This pairing is consistent on the temperature mechanism.

evidence: Subject: 'The gate's per-pass model ladder is likewise not in play: RunRequest carries no model-class field'
Subject: 'the split-brain risk recorded earlier on this ticket ... cannot arise on this path'
Prerequisite: '0d76 (parity bar) compares v1=Anthropic against v2=Bedrock. Without per-pass control the arms differ in TWO variables'
findings.finding: The prerequisite (per-pass model configuration seam) resolves the split-brain risk by making the gate steps DECLARE their class (frontier for Pass-1, standard for Pass-2/Pass-4), so a Bedrock gate run routes each pass to the intended Bedrock class. The subject plan explicitly REJECTS running the gate itself (`rebar review-plan`) as its instrument, and instead runs single-prompt eval cases through `run_case` with `gate_config`, arguing the per-pass model ladder 'is likewise not in play' because `RunRequest` carries no model-class field. This means the subject harness does NOT exercise the per-pass class-declaration mechanism the prerequisite delivers; it deliberately routes around it. This is a scope divergence, not a logical contradiction: the subject measures provider parity on a single-model path, while the prerequisite's per-pass seam governs the gate path S8 will actually use. The subject even names the same split-brain hazard the prerequisite fixes ('a bare claude-* ladder rung silently routing a Bedrock arm to direct Anthropic') and states it 'cannot arise on this path.' The two plans are consistent — the subject measures a narrower, deterministic path precisely so its parity finding is attributable, while acknowledging the gate's per-pass behaviour is the prerequisite's concern.
findings.location: Exactly one variable between the arms; Not a GitHub Actions job

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the parity_report caller enumeration: it is also called by parallel_run_and_diff (parity.py:329) and relocation_spot_eval (fidelity_spot_eval.py:194); restate the claim as 'no PRODUCTION/gate-op caller' rather than 'the only references are its definition and two internal reuses'.
evidence: Plan: 'under src/ the only references are its own definition and two internal reuses, container_fidelity_report and prerequisite_fidelity_report'

grep parity_report src/: parity.py:329 `return parity_report(v1, v2)` (parallel_run_and_diff); fidelity_spot_eval.py:194 `return parity.parity_report(v1, v2, min_gold=SPOT_MIN_GOLD)` (relocation_spot_eval)
The intended point — no production/gate-op caller — is not falsified; both are harness/eval callers
findings.finding: The plan asserts parity_report 'has ZERO production callers — under src/ the only references are its own definition and two internal reuses, container_fidelity_report and prerequisite_fidelity_report'. A grep of src/ refutes the enumeration: parity_report is ALSO called at src/rebar/llm/parity.py:329 (inside parallel_run_and_diff) and at src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:194 (inside relocation_spot_eval — the very spot-eval precedent this plan models itself on). The load-bearing claim (no PRODUCTION/gate-op caller, justifying net-new wiring) still holds — both omitted references are eval/harness infrastructure, not production gate ops — but the 'only references are X and Y' enumeration is incomplete as written.
findings.location: Plan §Approach, 'Correcting an earlier claim in this plan'
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer trusts the enumeration and misses that fidelity_spot_eval already exercises parity_report through a full paired path
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: 'parity_report has no production (gate-op) caller — under src/ its callers are its own two fidelity wrappers (container_fidelity_report, prerequisite_fidelity_report), parallel_run_and_diff, and the spot-eval precedent relocation_spot_eval; none is on the review/gate path.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the corpus-eligibility rule exclude container criteria (G3/G4/decomp-shape) whose dataset case lacks a non-empty `children:` payload — or replace the `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar` worked example with a case that actually runs — since childless container cases raise `ValueError` in `_run_criterion_case` before any model call.
evidence: `_run_criterion_case` at src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:110-116 raises `ValueError('container criterion needs a non-empty children list ...')` when a CONTAINER_CRITERIA criterion has no `children`.
pass1.CONTAINER_CRITERIA = ('G3','G4','decomp-shape') (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:46).

plan-review-container.eval.yaml `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar` (lines 85-94) carries `criterion: G3` and `input:` prose but NO `children:` key — so it raises; the plan's worked example claims it yields `ItemRecord(valid=True, decision='block', label='block')`, 'a recall hit, not a flip'.

The committed provider_parity_results.json records exactly those two container G3 cases as errored on both arms (lines 391-419, and its corpus_note admits n dropped 30→28), contradicting the plan's '30 items, 15 gold-block and 15 gold-advisory' claim.

decomp-shape cases DO carry `children:` (plan-review-decomp-shape.eval.yaml lines 45-50) and run, so the defect is specifically childless container cases the eligibility rule cannot detect by criterion id alone.
findings.finding: The corpus-eligibility rule admits container criteria (G3/G4) whose `run_case` arm raises `ValueError` for any case lacking a non-empty `children:` payload, but the pooled `plan-review-container` G3/G4 dataset cases carry only inline `input:` and no `children:`; the plan specifies no selection-time exclusion for these, so they error before any model call and the plan's own worked example asserting a valid G3 `block` record is impossible on this path.
findings.location: Approach → 'Corpus and the gold floor' (eligibility rule + the `G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar` worked example)
scenarios: Selecting the first finding/fail case per spec for plan-review-container picks a childless G3 case, which raises on every epoch of both arms and is silently downgraded to an errored pair, shrinking the certified gold set below the stated 30.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the eligibility predicate: a case whose resolved criterion is in `pass1.CONTAINER_CRITERIA` is eligible ONLY if the case carries a non-empty `children:` list; and re-derive the corpus counts (currently 30/15/15) after that exclusion so the stated gold balance matches what the selector can actually run.

findings.finding: The PAYLOAD PARITY and TOOL PARITY operator-attested acceptance criteria require capturing an outbound request per provider and comparing it field-by-field, but no described work in the Approach or Scope produces or captures those outbound requests — the Scope enumerates the probe, driver, adapter, serializer and CLI, none of which mention request capture or comparison.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — '[operator-attested] PAYLOAD PARITY is proven' and 'TOOL PARITY is proven'; Scope section
